text:
maya: Hey @sarah_peopleops quick Q — candidate is DE-based and manager wants them to start 2026-04-01. Benefits enrollment would normally kick in after a 90-day waiting period (so ~2026-07-01). Manager is asking if we can 1) enroll early or 2) provide a prorated benefits stipend while waiting. Offer is live: <https://redwood/offers/2065-129>. Any policy exceptions?

sarah_peopleops: Hey Maya — short answers first: in DE we generally can’t backdate statutory benefits (pension/health) because payroll/reporting/legal reqs. But we can do a temporary cash "benefits bridge" to cover out-of-pocket costs or mimic value, subject to Finance/Comp approvals. Need specifics: band, base, sign-on, requested stipend amount, and org code. Also if stipend > €2,000 total it needs comp committee review.

nate_talent: Candidate: Lina Müller. Band: IC3. Base: €95,000. Sign-on: €10,000 (proposed 60/40). Start requested: 2026-04-01. No relocation. Manager: @nate_talent noted they want benefits effective day 1 and would prefer stipend over delaying start.

jamal: FYI — DE payroll rules: employer contributions and statutory filings require registration and social security enrollment; cannot be backdated. Cash stipend OK but taxed as income. Finance needs to approve tax treatment and amount. If you want to structure a temporary monthly allowance instead of lump sum, that can be easier operationally.

offer-bot: Offer package uploaded: /offers/2065-129_Lina_Muller.pdf

sarah_peopleops: Proposed routing/process:
- People Ops: approve benefits-bridge policy exception (up to €2k total)
- Finance: sign-off on stipend amount and tax handling
- Compensation committee: required if stipend > €2k or sign-on structure changes
- Manager/Hiring: complete comp-exception form and attach offer + rationale.

Please fill the comp-exception form here: https://redwood.apps/comp-exception and tag @jamal for payroll.

maya: Manager proposes a bridge of €1,200/month for first 3 months (total €3,600) — manager requests to frontload €1,800 on first payroll and €900/month for next two months to help candidate with early medical costs.

nate_talent: Manager confirms the proposed split and is willing to escalate to comp committee if needed.

sarah_peopleops: Noted — because total > €2k this needs comp committee. ACTIONS:
- @maya please submit comp-exception with the exact wording for the offer letter
- @jamal will review payroll feasibility and tax treatment
- People Ops will queue comp committee review (48–72h turnaround typical)

Sample clause for offer letter (please paste into form):
```
Temporary benefits bridge: While statutory benefits enrollment is processed, the company will provide a temporary benefits stipend of €1,200/month for up to 3 months. The stipend is taxable and will be paid via payroll. This stipend is not a replacement for statutory employer contributions and is subject to normal payroll deductions.
```

jamal: Payroll note — if start = 2026-04-01, payroll cutoff is 2026-03-25. We need candidate gov ID, tax docs and org code by 2026-03-24 to include in first run. Also confirm whether you want stipend on first pay or split across runs.

maya: Filing comp-exception now. I put the proposed split and attached the offer PDF. Tagging @sarah_peopleops and @jamal.

sarah_peopleops: Thanks — once comp committee signs off we’ll update the offer letter language and notify Finance/Payroll. If committee denies, fallback is: delayed benefits start + larger sign-on installment subject to manager approval.

nate_talent: Sounds good. Will monitor and update candidate timeline. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all — will update thread after comp committee outcome. :calendar:
